sources.quote: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic благословити (blagosloviti), a calque of Ancient Greek ἐυλογεῖν (eulogeîn). By surface analysis, бла́го (bláho, “good”) + сло́во (slóvo, “word”) + -и́ти (-ýty). Compare Russian благослови́ть (blagoslovítʹ), Belarusian благаславі́ць (blahaslavícʹ).
sources.note: Wiktionary (en), CC BY-SA 4.0, автори статті — на сторінці; витяг Wiktextract/kaikki.org 2026-10-03

благословити.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic благословити (blagosloviti), a calque of Ancient Greek ἐυλογεῖν (eulogeîn). By surface analysis, бла́го (bláho, “good”) + сло́во (slóvo, “word”) + -и́ти (-ýty). Compare Russian благослови́ть (blagoslovítʹ), Belarusian благаславі́ць (blahaslavícʹ).

sources.quote: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic храмъ (xramŭ) via Old East Slavic храмъ (xramŭ). Doublet of хоро́м (xoróm) from хоромъ (xoromŭ). For sense as patrons saint's day, compare Romanian hram.

храм.text: Borrowed from Old Church Slavonic храмъ (xramŭ) via Old East Slavic храмъ (xramŭ). Doublet of хоро́м (xoróm) from хоромъ (xoromŭ). For sense as patrons saint's day, compare Romanian hram.

sources.quote: Borrowed from Old East Slavic Дунаи (Dunai), Дꙋнаи (Dunai), from Proto-Slavic *Dunavь, from Gothic *𐌳𐍉𐌽𐌰𐍅𐌹 (*dōnawi), from Proto-Germanic *Dōnawjaz, from Proto-Celtic *Dānowyos (whence also Danubius), an extended form of the river-name *Dānu, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂nu (“river goddess”)…
sources.note: Wiktionary (en), CC BY-SA 4.0, автори статті — на сторінці; витяг Wiktextract/kaikki.org 2026-10-03

Дунай.text: Borrowed from Old East Slavic Дунаи (Dunai), Дꙋнаи (Dunai), from Proto-Slavic *Dunavь, from Gothic *𐌳𐍉𐌽𐌰𐍅𐌹 (*dōnawi), from Proto-Germanic *Dōnawjaz, from Proto-Celtic *Dānowyos (whence also Danubius), an extended form of the river-name *Dānu, from Proto-Indo-European *déh₂nu (“river goddess”), akin to *dʰenh₂- (“to set in motion; to flow”).
